dhcp_confirm.title: Set up the discovered Tuxedo Touch
dhcp_confirm.description: A Tuxedo Touch panel at {host} took a DHCP lease with MAC address {mac}. Enter the panel's web login credentials (not your 4-digit keypad user code, unless your installer set them to match) to add it. The address comes from the lease, so it is not asked for; the panel is identified by its MAC address from here on and a later lease change is followed automatically.

data_description.use_https: Required if 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the unit (the common/default state).
data_description.username: The unit's web login username (touchscreen: Settings -> Login settings), not the keypad code.
data_description.code: Optional. Used as the default arm/disarm code so automations can arm without prompting.
data_description.partition: The panel partition this entry controls. Discovery offers a panel once; a second partition is added with 'Add integration' and picks up the panel's MAC address from the next lease.
data_description.port: The web server port on the unit. 443 with HTTPS enabled (the default state), 80 without.

user.title: Connect to Tuxedo Touch
user.description: Enter the panel's web login credentials (not your 4-digit keypad user code, unless your installer set them to match).

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Tuxedo Touch unit on your LAN. A panel added by hand is identified by this address until Home Assistant sees its DHCP lease, so give it a static IP or DHCP reservation.
data_description.use_https: Required if 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the unit (the common/default state).
data_description.username: The unit's web login username (touchscreen: Settings -> Login settings), not the keypad code.
data_description.code: Optional. Used as the default arm/disarm code so automations can arm without prompting.
data_description.partition: The panel partition this entry controls.
data_description.port: The web server port on the unit. 443 with HTTPS enabled (the default state), 80 without.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate Tuxedo Touch
reauth_confirm.description: The panel at {host} rejected the stored web login credentials. Enter the current ones.

data_description.username: The web login username from the touchscreen's Login settings.
data_description.password: The web login password for that account.

reauth_retry.title: Try the stored credentials once more
reauth_retry.description: These are the credentials the panel at {host} refused, so Home Assistant will not send them again on its own. Submit this only if something has changed at the panel - most often re-enabling web access for this user on the touchscreen under Setup, then Users/Account, Enable All, Apply. Submitting sends exactly one login. Three refused web logins disable every web account, on unpatched firmware permanently and clearable only at the touchscreen. If the password itself was changed at the keypad, go back and enter the new one instead.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Tuxedo Touch
reconfigure.description: Change the panel's address, port, credentials, keypad code or partition. Leave the password and keypad code blank to keep the stored ones.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Tuxedo Touch unit on your LAN. A panel added by hand is identified by this address until Home Assistant sees its DHCP lease, so give it a static IP or DHCP reservation.
data_description.use_https: Required if 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the unit (the common/default state).
data_description.username: The unit's web login username (touchscreen: Settings -> Login settings), not the keypad code.
data_description.password: The unit's web login password. Blank keeps the stored password.
data_description.code: Optional. Used as the default arm/disarm code so automations can arm without prompting. Blank keeps the stored code.
data_description.partition: The panel partition this entry controls.
data_description.port: The web server port on the unit. 443 with HTTPS enabled (the default state), 80 without.

error.invalid_auth: Invalid username or password. If the panel was recently reset, web access may have been disabled for this user - re-enable it on the touchscreen under Setup -> Account.
error.possibly_locked_out: The panel is refusing credentials that previously worked. Either the web password was changed at the keypad, or the panel has disabled its web accounts after repeated failed logins. On unpatched firmware that lockout is permanent and clears only at the touchscreen: Setup, then Users/Account, re-enable web access, Enable All, Apply. On patched firmware it clears itself after five minutes, so wait five minutes and try once - each further guess is another failed login.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect - check the IP/port and that the unit is reachable. The panel serves only ONE connection at a time, so close any browser tab open to it and retry.
error.panel_error: The panel answered but the response could not be used. See the Home Assistant log for the specific reason.
error.unknown: Unexpected error - see the Home Assistant log for the traceback

abort.already_in_progress: This panel is already being set up.

no_code.message: No alarm code provided and none configured for this panel.

command_not_carried_out.message: The panel did not carry out the command: it reports {reported} where {requested} was asked for. Arm and disarm answer without saying whether the panel acted, so this is the status poll's own reading afterwards. A faulted zone refuses an arm, and a code the panel does not accept refuses a disarm; the alarm entity keeps showing what the panel reports.

auth_failed.message: The panel rejected the stored web login credentials: {error}

credentials_rejected_no_retry.message: The panel rejected the stored web login credentials, so Home Assistant has deliberately stopped attempting logins: repeated failed web logins can disable the panel's web accounts, permanently on unpatched firmware. Enter the current credentials on the re-authentication card and Home Assistant will try again then, once.

update_failed.message: Could not read the panel's status: {error}

status_not_available.message: The panel answered 'Not available' rather than a security status. This is a quirk of the panel's own firmware and not a connection problem; the alarm stays unavailable until the panel reports a real status, which it does on its own.

https_required.message: The panel redirected the API call to HTTPS. Turn on 'Use HTTPS' for this entry; the repair notification does it for you.

confirm.title: Switch {title} to HTTPS
confirm.description: 'Secured Web Server Access' is enabled on the panel, so it redirects every plain-HTTP API call to HTTPS and arming, disarming and status all fail. Submitting this turns on 'Use HTTPS' for this entry, moves port 80 to 443 (port {port} stays as it is if it is anything else) and reloads the integration.

abort.entry_gone: That Tuxedo Touch entry no longer exists, so there is nothing left to switch.

duplicate_entry.title: Two Tuxedo Touch entries reach one panel
duplicate_entry.description: {title} and {other} both reach the same panel and partition, so only one of them can hold the panel's identity. Remove whichever entry you do not want under Settings > Devices & services; the other adopts the panel's MAC address on the panel's next DHCP lease.

credentials_rejected.title: Tuxedo Touch is refusing the stored credentials
credentials_rejected.description: {title} logged in with these web credentials before and the panel now refuses them, so Home Assistant has stopped trying: three failed web logins disable every web account on unpatched firmware, with no timeout, and only the touchscreen can re-enable them (Setup, then Users/Account, re-enable web access, Enable All, Apply). The likely cause is a web password changed at the keypad. Enter the current credentials on this entry's re-authentication card - one attempt, not a series of guesses. If the panel refuses credentials you are sure of, its accounts are already disabled and the touchscreen is the only way back.
